items.title: Dev Feedback | Nov 25
items.summary: Dear Pathfinders, Good to see you again for the latest Dev Feedback installment! How have your adventures across Idyll been lately? The community has had a lot to say since the recent update, some of it appreciative and plenty of it pointed
items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

Good to see you again for the latest Dev Feedback installment! How have your adventures across Idyll been lately?

The community has had a lot to say since the recent update, some of it appreciative and plenty of it pointed, and the team has been following up on all of it. For this issue of Dev Feedback, we’ve gathered the questions that came up most and drew the most attention, along with our thinking and our plans for each.

We’re answering 9 questions this time. Some are pain points where the experience still needs work, while others stem from things we didn’t fully consider in the initial design. We’ve talked them over internally, worked out what we want to change and when, and wanted to share that with you right away.

Here’s what’s in this issue of Dev Feedback:

Q1: In Home events, the Pumpkin Aeon and Park order submissions both mean carrying items back and forth between your Home and the warehouse. It’s a tedious process—but will it be improved?

This comes down to a technical limitation. Data doesn’t pass between the two scenes, and because your Home runs a production simulation, that data genuinely can’t sync to the outside scene in real time. We’re working to let you view and submit Park orders from inside your Home as soon as we can, and we expect it to go live in 1.1.2.

Q2: The Nighttime Gathering needs a team if you want furniture blueprints at any reasonable speed. Isn’t that too high a bar for solo players?

This one is a social event, yes—but since everyone plays differently, we put the rarest reward, the RV skin, on the personal progress track, and we stretched the event from the two weeks originally planned out to four. Playing solo, you can still earn every core reward under your own steam, so take part at whatever pace suits you.

Q3: Wishstars have been in short supply for so long, and reaching 70,000 Contribution points for the Platform is difficult. It’s a lot of pressure. Are there plans to change this?

Here’s a tip. You can raise your Platform’s Contribution points by spending season currency on season furniture. Season furniture converts its Comfort value into Contribution at a 3x ratio, which is far more efficient than regular furniture, so there’s no need to grind away at Wishstars.

Q4: Getting matched with players using cheat software in Egg Heist PvP ruins the experience. What’s being done about it?

We have zero tolerance for cheating. Here’s what’s in place right now:

1. Automated detection. The system locates and bans cheaters the moment it spots them.

2. An open reporting channel. Please report any suspected cheaters you encounter to help us target the right accounts.

3. Ongoing fixes for the exploits and bugs that cheat software relies on.

Egg Heist PvP is also still in its test period. We’ll be iterating on the mode as a whole using this season’s data, and the changes already planned include:

  • Improving battlefield maps and fixing the exploits that let players gain an unfair advantage

    [/*]

  • Toning down the excessive survivability and healing on certain Aniimo, so lineups stop converging on the same few picks

    [/*]

  • Adding respawn protection, so nobody has to put up with being camped at the spawn point

    [/*]

Q5: How does balancing work in modes like Egg Heist PvP and friendly matches?

To keep competition fair, these rules apply once you’re in:

1. The system keeps your Aniimo’s species, form, appearance and skill set, and builds a temporary lineup from them.

2. Progression attributes such as level, personality, acquired potential, resonance and capability are standardized to the fair-play template.

3. Held Items are kept and set to a uniform level, their base attributes standardized, with their core and advanced effects active.

4. Core skill enhancements are switched off across the board.

5. On top of those standardized numbers, each Aniimo gets its own attribute adjustments, and that’s how we balance the strength differences between them.

Q6: I’m at 300 stars in Egg Emperor and still haven’t pulled the Evercrystal Egg. What do I do if I can’t complete the collection before the season ends?

We’re making adjustments to the difficulty of obtaining collectibles and to their drop rates in stages. High-Rank Guarantee: At 200 stars in Egg Emperor there’s now a pick-your-own collectible feature, guaranteeing you one specific collectible you’re missing. Weekly Guarantee: The Egg Heist Shop now stocks a collectible blind box that Egg Emperor players can buy once a week, guaranteeing one random collectible. Rate-Up Event: Version 1.1.2 sees the launch of a collectible rate-up event that sharply raises every collectible drop rate in Operation: Egg Heist Team Mode. System Improvements: Season 2 sees the launch of more collectible events, aimed squarely at how random acquisition feels right now and at duplicates being useless at present. Season Reruns: After Season 1 ends there will be rerun modes and events to help you keep working on this season’s collectibles.

Q7: The reward gap between multiplayer and solo in Aniimo Dash is large, and solo players clearly earn far more slowly. Will the ratio between the two be adjusted?

It will. The 1.1.2 update on November 26 adds weekly quests to Aniimo Dash’s solo mode. After that, playing solo will earn you a reliable supply of Racing Coins each week.

Q8: There aren’t many Aniimo with Level 3 Pathfinding abilities or Level 3 flight abilities. Will there be more options for exploring with our favorite Aniimo?

In an upcoming version we’re raising the flight ability of Prismana Hypnyto and Prismana Ekrim to Level 3. We’ll also be adding more Aniimo with high-level Pathfinding and with entirely new exploration abilities, so you have more to choose from.

Q9: After the major version update, the extra report reward for catching an Aniimo on the first try was removed, which lowered the overall rewards from catching Aniimo. Free-to-play players are having a hard time saving Credits, and it’s now harder to exchange for Aniipods and Capability Reset Cards. How will this be adjusted?

We’ve noticed this issue. Removing that mechanic did lower some players’ rewards. So we’re raising the base report Credit reward from 1,200 to 1,600 to cover that gap and ease the pressure on Credits.

That’s everything for this issue of Dev Feedback. Thank you again for all the questions and suggestions. The gripes, the hopes, and the long, carefully written feedback posts, we’ve read every one of them. The questions in this issue were picked from the threads that drew the most discussion, and we’ll keep Dev Feedback going to follow up on the topics you care about.

If there’s something you’d like us to answer, leave a comment or make a post under the relevant topic. We collect and sort through all feedback and add it to the pool for future issues, and we’ll do our best to get back to you promptly. We’d also love to hear how you’re finding the game, whether that’s something that felt rough or a surprise you stumbled on mid-adventure. It all gets read.

Lastly, we hope every one of you has a wonderful time adventuring across Idyll.

The Aniimo Team

Dear Pathfinders,

The Polaris Institute plans to take the servers offline for maintenance and an update on November 26, 2026. You won’t be able to log in during maintenance, so please plan your adventures accordingly.

Read on for an overview of this update!

I. Maintenance Schedule

\

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/26 06:00 ~ 11:00 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/26 02:00 ~ 07:00 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/26 14:00 ~ 19:00 UTC+8

\ Glimmer ×500

\ Pathfinders who complete registration before the Season 2 update

※ Maintenance may take more or less time than scheduled. Thank you for your understanding. Once maintenance ends, restart the game client to ensure you’re running the latest version.

II. New Content Preview

Key Gameplay Changes

To give you earlier access to the maps, Aniimo, and stories of the Whisperwake Isles and smooth out the steep climb from Lv. 40 to 55, we’ve lowered the entry levels for content across the isles and adjusted the related systems.

Story Quest Level Changes

1. We’ve lowered the requirements to accept the Whisperwake Isles main quest "A Tale of Tide and Song." Pathfinders now meet its level and title requirements once they reach Lv. 50 and advance to Wayfarer III.

※ After the update, Pathfinders who have completed the Breezy Plains main quest "A New Journey" and meet the requirements above will automatically receive the Whisperwake Isles main quest "A Song from the Sea."

2. We’ve lowered the requirements to accept "Rainbow of the Ground," the final chapter of the Breezy Plains main questline. Your character now needs to reach Lv. 45 and advance to Wayfarer II.

Map Level Changes

We’ve lowered the levels of some areas in the Breezy Plains and Whisperwake Isles, and reduced the levels and difficulty of some Alphas and Omegas.

\

1. Breezy Plains – Tideblossom Coast: lowered to Lv. 52–57.

2. Whisperwake Isles – Crescent Bay: lowered to Lv. 50–55.

3. Whisperwake Isles – Rosy Mirelands: lowered to Lv. 56–58.

4. Whisperwake Isles – Wildwater Gorge: lowered to Lv. 57–59.

5. Whisperwake Isles – Cloudreach Falls: lowered to Lv. 58–60.

\

1. Infergon Omega: lowered to Lv. 48.

2. Luminelle Alpha: lowered to Lv. 57.

3. Glameep Alpha: lowered to Lv. 55.

4. Sugartini Alpha: lowered to Lv. 58.

5. Jabster Alpha: lowered to Lv. 59.

6. Jeburst Omega: lowered to Lv. 60.

Safaris Required for Leveling

We’ve reduced the number of Safaris required to level up from Lv. 41 through 54. After the update, Pathfinders affected by this change will receive compensation via in-game mail.

Pathfinder Challenge Level Changes

We’ve lowered the levels and difficulty of some Pathfinder Challenges in the Whisperwake Isles.

Title Promotion and Elite Training Changes

1. After the update, Pathfinders working through the sixth chapter of Elite Training’s "Chapter of Breezy" can continue the story. Once they reach the Whisperwake Isles, they can unlock "Chapter of Whisperwake" and take on its challenges.

2. If you’ve completed the Chapter 1 Elite Training quests in "Chapter of Whisperwake" and want to continue with Title Promotion, follow the guidance back to Chapter 6 of "Chapter of Breezy" and complete its challenges. Once you reach Grade I Trailblazer, you can resume Title Promotion in "Chapter of Whisperwake."

New Story Quest

"Hymn of Calm"

The Sanctum has reappeared, life has returned, and the great tree atop the mountain has suddenly grown. Overjoyed, the family of Dewlops born around the Sanctum wants to offer the Hymn of Calm to the Sanctum.

Where did the melody etched into their souls come from, and what does the song flowing through their hearts tell? Calm and storm each have a story of their own.

New Events

"Fantasy Resonance"

\

"Aniimo-Europe" After the update ~ 2026/12/17 03:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" After the update ~ 2026/12/17 03:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" After the update ~ 2026/12/17 03:59 UTC+8

\

Advance your character to Student I.

\

1. During the event, a group of Jaguaraun will appear on the Continent of Idyll every day at 04:00. Complete designated tasks in "Fantasy Investigation" to claim the corresponding rewards.

※ In Companion Mode, Jaguaraun caught by friends also count toward progress on the relevant catching tasks.

2. Complete all "Fantasy Investigation" tasks to claim the Offering Recipe for the featured Aniimo.

3. Complete the designated task in each round of "Fantasy Investigation" to claim Fantasy Token ×1.

4. If you missed an earlier event, spend one Fantasy Token at the Event Vendor to get one Offering Recipe for an Aniimo from a past round. Check the Event Vendor’s listings for what’s available.

"Annual Carnival"

\

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/27 10:00 ~ 2026/12/01 12:00 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/27 10:00 ~ 2026/12/01 12:00 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/27 10:00 ~ 2026/12/01 12:00 UTC+8

\

Advance your character to Student I.

\

1. During the event, claim rewards such as appearance discount vouchers and random treasure chests on the event page each day.

2. After logging in during the event, go to Shop > Pack to claim a free Aniimo Gratitude Gift Box. It contains Departure with the Wind: Collectible Blind Box ×1, Wonder Sugar Crystal ×100, and Vein Essence ×5.

3. Special Annual Carnival bundles will be available in the Pack section. They contain items for "Splendorweave," the new item Renewal Pigment, Prismatic Orb, and more.

※ Using Renewal Pigment guarantees one Sparkling Pigment you don’t already own, excluding Shadow Sparkling and Dazzling Sparkling varieties.

4. During the event, spend enough Lumin Crystals to reach a reward tier, then claim the corresponding Starlight Reward on the "Starlight Echoes" event page.

※ The event preview will be available in Events on November 26.

"Starlight Echoes"

\

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/27 10:00 ~ 2026/12/01 12:00 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/27 10:00 ~ 2026/12/01 12:00 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/27 10:00 ~ 2026/12/01 12:00 UTC+8

\

Advance your character to Student I.

\

1. Lumin Crystals you spend during the event count toward cumulative event progress.

2. Once your total Lumin Crystals spent reaches a specified tier, claim the corresponding Starlight Reward on the "Starlight Echoes" event page.

"Return to Idyll"

\

You must meet all the following conditions.

1. Your character has advanced to Student I.

2. You have not logged in for at least 14 consecutive days.

3. At least 42 days have passed since you last activated "Return to Idyll."

\

The event starts automatically when an eligible Pathfinder logs in and ends at 04:00 on the 15th day after activation.

\

1. "7-Day Gift"

Log in each day during the event to claim rewards. Rewards fall into two tiers based on consecutive days away: 14 days or 30 days.

2. "Return Journey"

Complete designated tasks to earn Reunion Tokens and a Double-Cost Ticket (7 Days). Collect the required number of Reunion Tokens to claim Glimmer rewards. Collect 1,350 Reunion Tokens to claim an additional Prismana Egg of Choice ×1.

3. "Reunion Blessing"

During the event, when returning Pathfinders team up with other Pathfinders, both can share the following benefits.

1. Rewards from Friends’ Companion Mode Reports increase by 20%.

2. Rewards from Friends’ shared Prismatic Energy increase by 20%.

3. The chance of successfully catching Aniimo in Companion Mode increases by 10%.

※ The buff does not stack when there is more than one returning Pathfinder in the same party.

※ If there are both new and returning Pathfinders in the same party, their buffs are identical and do not stack.

"Aniimo Dash"

\

Prismana Eggs have been added to the shop rewards.

\

Four Weekly Quests have been added.

1. Like other Pathfinders 10 times in Group Races.

2. Use items a total of 10 times in Group Races.

3. Complete one Solo Race.

4. Earn an A grade or higher once in a Solo Race.

\

Group Race now tracks your best placement.

※ Best placements will be recorded starting after this update.

New Appearances

New Prismatic Appearances

"Dawn Radiance"

Day breaks in a blaze of light, bathing the clear skies in morning radiance.

"Moonshadow Starlight"

Moonshadows fall and starlight swirls, drawing all into a night of quiet dreams.

Both appearances are available through "Splendorweave."

III. Improvements and Adjustments

Progression Changes

1. Gracewing Limited-Time Reset

\ The reset applies to Gracewing obtained before this balance update in any of its listed forms: Basic Form/Sea of Flowers Form/Nighttime Form/Mountain Woods Form.

\

All EXP Items used will be refunded, and the corresponding EXP will be deducted.

Star Up will be reset to its initial state, and all materials used will be refunded.

Capability Awakening will be reset to its initial state, and all materials used will be refunded.

Capafruit will be refunded, uses will become available again, and the effects will be removed.

\

"Aniimo-Europe" After the update ~ 2026/12/10 20:00:00 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" After the update ~ 2026/12/10 16:00:00 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" After the update ~ 2026/12/11 4:00:00 UTC+8

Story Experience

1. Added story voice-over to Home progression quests.

2. Added story voice-over to Title Promotion quests.

Homeland

1. The largest RV model now unlocks at Lv. 16. You can change your RV skin once the RV reaches Lv. 16.

2. Rain now waters crops at Home automatically without any action from you or your Aniimo.

3. Improved furniture placement when building. If there’s flooring at the default placement spot, furniture automatically snaps up to floor height.

4. Limited-Time Home Shop Stock

\

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/27 04:00 ~ 2026/12/02 03:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/27 04:00 ~ 2026/12/02 03:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/27 04:00 ~ 2026/12/02 03:59 UTC+8

\

During the event, selected items can be redeemed for a limited time under Resource Exchange in the Home Shop.

Operation: Egg Heist

1. Double Collectible Drop Rates for a Limited Time

\

"Aniimo-Europe" After the update ~ 2026/12/09 23:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" After the update ~ 2026/12/09 23:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" After the update ~ 2026/12/09 23:59 UTC+8

\

During the event, in Operation: Egg Heist Team Mode at any difficulty, the drop rates of both common collectibles and prized collectibles from opening treasure chests or defeating Umbral Aniimo increase by 100%.

2. Added the "Prismatic Iris · Dark" collectible to Chaos mode in Operation: Egg Heist Team Mode.

3. Improved how you pick up and swap items when your Inventory is full.

4. Improved how Pathfinder names are displayed in Fair Arena.

System and Feature Improvements

1. Improved camera behavior in the Appearance interface.

2. Updated the icons and order of Inventory tabs and added an "Available" tab separate from Common Items.

3. To make Nurture easier, you can no longer place Mark Sharing markers within range of a Bloom.

4. You can now view network status in the Function Menu. If you run into problems in multiplayer, use the Function Menu to check your network connection.

5. Added an "Apply Face Data" option to Outfit Settings in the Appearance interface.

6. Items on cooldown now show a cooldown indicator.

7. Improved item locking. You can now check whether an item is locked and unlock it directly from the item-use screen.

8. The purchase limit is now displayed directly on the icons of items with purchase limits.

9. Improved information display and the process of applying an appearance in the Appearance interface.

10. You can now select a teammate’s current location on the map and initiate a teleport.

11. You can now switch to Aniimo at Home in the Aniimo Accessories interface.

12. Your Profile now lets you hide the interface and share your profile.

13. Your Profile now shows separate counts for Aniimo with three maxed attributes and Aniimo with six maxed attributes.

14. Hid prompts for interacting with other Pathfinders near the Research Console so it’s easier to submit reports.

15. ChillBeanz in Astra now serves Iced Coffee Fizz. Drinking it restores 300 Ultimate Points to the Team. It can only be used while freely exploring the Continent of Idyll and has a 30-second cooldown.

Mobile Improvements

1. Improved map zoom.

2. Improved download speeds on Android devices.

3. Improved how the hatching interface displays on some devices.

IV. Bug Fixes

Aniimo and Combat

1. Fixed a mismatch between the actual effect of Hoptail’s "Tail Flick Combo" and its skill description.

2. Fixed an issue where Scrubbit’s "Rain-Pond Leaf Strike" failed to reduce healing as intended.

3. Fixed an issue with the healing radius of "Help! Gracewing!"

4. Fixed an animation issue when catching some Aniimo.

5. Fixed an issue where Dazmand’s "Spotlight Moment" trait sometimes failed to trigger on first entering the field, causing its first skill to still consume Energy.

6. Fixed an issue where Coraliz sometimes failed to recover Energy when its "Coral Spike" mark was removed.

System and Feature Fixes

1. Fixed a display issue with the "Plains Swiftsong" chat bubble.

2. Fixed overlapping Aniimo models in the pop-up in the Illusory Aniimo interface.

3. Fixed a pop-up text display issue when switching groups.

4. Fixed a display issue with the "Freshly Hatched Partner" buff icon.

5. Fixed incorrect Aniimo gender display when entering Aniimo Exchange.

6. Made the enlarged preview size consistent with other screens when viewing or sending images in chat.

7. Fixed party invitations in a channel expiring too quickly.

8. Fixed the Flute Call sound effect cutting off before the end.

9. Fixed the Acquired Potential grade display failing to update after separating an Aniimo’s Training and Acquired Potential in Aniimo Exchange.

10. Fixed an issue that sometimes prevented the chat notification dot from clearing.

Homeland

1. Fixed an issue in "Nighttime Gathering" that prevented switching quests when no quests could be accepted.

2. Fixed incorrect quality ratings for some Home items.

3. Fixed a Load limit that wasn’t enforced when using Sets at a Park.

4. Fixed the background of the notification that appears when crops mutate.

5. Fixed an issue where searching for furniture could incorrectly trigger the word filter.

6. Fixed the reward notification dot failing to appear in the Home Index after collecting a complete furniture set.

Console Fixes

1. Fixed a prolonged black screen when opening the RV interface at Home on PS5 and Xbox.

2. Fixed video freezing and failing to play after returning to the login screen on PS5.

3. Fixed stuttering when opening the Warehouse or performing batch actions at Home on PS5 and Xbox.

4. Fixed stuttering when sorting Aniimo in Aniimo Management on PS5 and Xbox.

5. Fixed stuttering when releasing Aniimo on PS5 and Xbox.

6. Fixed frame drops and lightning effects displaying incorrectly in Aniimo Dash on PS5 and Xbox.

Mobile Fixes

1. Fixed stuttering and frame drops in some situations on the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra.

2. Fixed vegetation disappearing near the Infergon Alpha on some devices.

3. Fixed racing smoke failing to obscure vision on some devices.

4. Fixed unexpected game client restarts when downloading in the background on some Android devices.

— Polaris Institute Operations Team

Dear Pathfinders,

The Polaris Institute plans to carry out server maintenance for an update on November 12, 2026. You will be unable to log in during maintenance, so please plan your adventures accordingly.

Here is a preview of what’s coming in this update!

I. Maintenance Schedule

\

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/12 06:00 ~ 11:00 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/12 02:00 ~ 07:00 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/12 14:00 ~ 19:00 UTC+8

\ Glimmer × 500

\ Pathfinders who registered before the Season 2 version update

※The actual maintenance duration may vary depending on progress. Thank you for your understanding. Once maintenance is complete, please restart the game client to ensure that you are running the latest version.

II. New Content Preview

New Story Quests

\

Two new Journey Quests will be added to Crescent Bay:

1. "The Coral Sea of Dreams": Reefish is always dreaming of a distant, tranquil coral sea. A paradise reachable only by crossing tidal storms—why have you chosen this fish, and how can it find you?

2. "Squarrel’s Poem of Revolution": Chompy the Squarrel has been turning Mirrorsea Village upside down... She means well, of course... But how can we get her to settle down? Her human partner, Dora, may know something.

Major Feature Updates

\

\

Aniimo Affinity is now available. Increase an Aniimo’s Affinity level to unlock the following benefits:

1. Unlock the ability to rename that Aniimo.

2. Increase the effects of the active skills "Heal" and "Swoleshroom" on that Aniimo.

You can increase Aniimo Affinity in the following ways:

1. Place the Aniimo in your Party or Home to gradually gain Affinity.

2. Use the Star Up and Ascend features on the Aniimo.

3. Complete Pathfinder Challenges and take part in Operation: Egg Heist with the Aniimo.

4. Defeat wild Aniimo and Alphas in Idyll with the Aniimo.

※Each Aniimo has daily and weekly limits on Affinity gains. Please plan their development accordingly.

Dear Pathfinders:

The sound of tides echoes, the distant isles are awakening, and the next stop of the journey has already arrived.

Polaris Institute plans to carry out a server maintenance update from 07:00 to 15:00 UTC+8 on October 29, 2026. During maintenance, you will not be able to log in to the game. Pathfinders, please plan your adventure time accordingly.

Below is an overview of this update. Please check it.

I. Maintenance Schedule

\

「Aniimo-Europe」2026/10/28 22:00~2026/10/29 7:00 (UTC+0)

「Aniimo-Americas」2026/10/28 19:00~2026/10/29 3:00 (UTC-4)

「Aniimo-Apac」2026/10/29 07:00~2026/10/29 15:00 (UTC+8)

\ 「Glimmer」× 500

\ Pathfinders who completed registration before the S2 season version update

※The actual duration of this maintenance may change depending on maintenance status. Thank you for your understanding. After maintenance is complete, please restart the game client to ensure the game is on the latest version.

II. New Content Preview

New Aniimo Debut

This version adds 51 brand-new Aniimo to the Idyll Continent. At the same time, Aniimo with multiple new Prismana Forms will appear across the world, awaiting Pathfinders' exploration and discovery~

\

Jeburst, Glameep, Pouchwisp, and Royalby—4 brand-new season-exclusive Prismana Aniimo. Don't miss them~

\

New Prismana Forms of Gachapus, Sugartini, Jabster, and Whirlbite appear in their corresponding areas across Whisperwake Isles, awaiting discovery and capture by Pathfinders.

\

Wind-element DPS Hypnyto joins the Idyll Continent—with the unique ability to control enemies to move along with itself, and can release small-area traps that deal continuous damage.

※Obtain Hypnyto and its Prismana Form through the Companion Handbook.

\

The Dark-element Breaker "Prismana Eklue," with both enemy-gathering and lifesteal DPS capabilities, officially debuts.

\

The first Pathfinder co-created Aniimo, Jaguaraun, a powerful and cool Lightning-element Breaker, is ready to set out!

New Map Region

As the adventure unfolds, Pathfinders will discover and set foot on the isolated Whisperwake Isles. This island cluster surrounded by the ocean has brand-new geography and is home to Aniimo of all shapes and forms. Here, Pathfinders can explore the interesting ecology and habits of Aniimo, catch new Aniimo as companions, open a new story chapter, and uncover the long-buried secrets of Whisperwake Isles.

Whisperwake Isles will open 4 map regions this time:

Crescent Bay—Giant bubbles like a crystalline dream gently embrace the lone tree in the middle of the lake. The Bubbeep family drifts leisurely by the lake surface of the moon bay. In the peaceful and relaxed Mirrorsea Village on the cliff, the islanders and Aniimo live together in harmony.

Rosy Mirelands—The river nourishes lush wetlands and woodlands. The wondrous slime of the Sugarfish family adds dreamy colors to the riverbanks, while also troubling other Aniimo living in the wetlands.

Wildwater Gorge—This is a gorge through which rushing rapids roar. Tempered by the currents, Aniimo full of power and energy live among the rapids and rocks. The Saws family rides the waves through the surging waters, while the Prawnch family treats this place as a natural training ground.

Cloudreach Falls—Lake water at the top of the cliff overflows from cracks, creating a spectacular waterfall. Beneath the huge drop of water, only Aniimo that never give up can climb the sky-reaching waterfall. Together with the Jeglid family, go upstream, explore the cliff covered by the waterfall, and keep climbing upward with the perseverance to reach the highest waterfall.

New Story Quests

\

Pathfinders will be guided by a wondrous song, swept into the waves, and arrive at the isolated Whisperwake Isles. Here, together with the little Aniimo Lyrelle and the youth Thesseo, begin a journey of pilgrimage and trials.

※After completing the prerequisite story quests, Whisperwake Isles-related content will automatically unlock.

\

New narrative-themed Journey Quests for Crescent Bay and Skytear Rift have been added, unfolding several warm little stories around the lives and bonds of Aniimo families such as Bubbeep, Salabask, Sugarfish, and Eko.

1. "Tale of Salabask Forest": The Salabask of Rosy Mirelands encounter a slime crisis, but their boss Lailai has turned into a talking Aniimo Egg? Pathfinders follow the trail and embark on an adventure to find the truth and friendship.

2. "The Rumored Seventh Princess": Princess, you are so beautiful, you are so kind, you are the most trusted friend of the Sugarfish, and the only star of the Guru Theater. Pathfinders are dragged into the performance in a daze—how will this messy Guru Theater end?

3. "Proof of the Rapids": According to the youth Thesseo, Skytear Rift has a legend of three challenges involving the rapids. How are these challenges completed, and where did they come from? Only truly powerful Pathfinders can find the answer.

4. "Who Moved the Golden Honey": Something big has happened—the golden honey of the Royalby has been stolen! Clever Pathfinder, there is only one truth!

5. "Itsy": The timid Lilipole Itsy doesn't dare to dance with everyone, doesn't dare to spray water to clean the mud, doesn't dare to... there are too many things it doesn't dare to do. How can it find courage...

\

1. "Coral Sea of Dreams": Reefish always loves to dream, and in its dreams there is a distant, peaceful coral sea. The ideal land that can only be reached by crossing tidal storms—why did you choose this fish, and how can the fish see you?

2. "Poem of Revolution": Many messy things have happened in Mirrorsea Village recently. Who is causing trouble? Or rather, who wants to make trouble...

3. "Ode to Tranquility": Della, the leader of the Dewlop family, wants to offer an "Ode to Tranquility" for the "Miracle of the Temple and the Great Tree," but this song has long been lost, and even Della herself cannot remember all of it. Pathfinders help collect the scattered melodies, complete the score, and uncover the story behind this song.

4. "Golden Treasure": Robin the Ekrim held a treasure hunt game, and the Eko played with great joy. But Robin's own treasure disappeared during the game...

\

New Journey Journal content related to Whisperwake Isles and Mirrorsea Village has been added. Pathfinders can unlock and view it by completing the related story quests.

New Growth Stage

Polaris Institute has taken note of the achievements made by Pathfinders. Dr. Lewis will contact Pathfinders at level 60 or higher to open new title promotion assessments: "Trailblazer II," "Trailblazer III," and Badge Challenges.

Elite Training unlocks the new "Chapter of Whisperwake." It can be challenged after the character's title reaches "Trailblazer I" and the Whisperwake Isles story quests have been advanced.

After title promotion, new character and Aniimo growth stages will be unlocked simultaneously:

1. "Trailblazer II": Aniimo level cap 60→65;

2. "Trailblazer III": Character level cap 65→70, Aniimo level cap 65→70.

3. Unlock new character Active Skills and Passive Talents.

Gameplay Season Update

"Operation: Egg Heist"

A new fair competitive PVP mode enters testing—3 teams compete for the Giga-Egg!

\ After the version update, daily 18:00 ~ 24:00

\

Character reaches level 50, Egg Heist rank reaches Rising Egg Scout

\

On a mysterious island, the dormant Giga-Egg awaits awakening! Three teams engage in fierce competition: fight for the sole Legendary Giga-Egg. Maintaining Twine with the Egg accumulates the Giga-Egg's activation value. When the Giga-Egg's activation value reaches 100% or the match ends, the team currently in Twine with the Giga-Egg wins. Victory is undecided until the final second—do your utmost to seize the Twine ownership of the Giga-Egg!

※This mode does not allow equipment loadouts to be configured or items to be brought in, and the stats of deployed Aniimo will be subject to balance adjustments.

※This gameplay is currently in testing and will be optimized and adjusted based on actual experience.

\

All members of the winning team will receive 1 "Giga-Egg," which guarantees an Umbral Egg and has a small chance to produce a Prismana Egg.

Each team that accumulates a certain activation value with the Giga-Egg can receive a reward Chest at the end, with a chance to produce season Collectibles.

\

Basic Collectibles:

1. Prismatic Iris: Among the gorgeous iris petals, prismatic colors sway. That brilliant thought rests gently in the soft embrace of the flower bud, peacefully awaiting the moment of bloom.

2. Butterfly Dream Amber: Treasured dreams flicker faintly within the crystal. Those irreplaceable moments have not faded in the slightest, as if even time cannot bear to flow on.

3. Ironhelm Shieldguard: Build fear into a solid wall, and turn cowardice into the courage to protect. The hardest enemy to defeat is always the timid self.

4. Songbird Serenade: The mountain wind whistles, the waves beat the rhythm, and the lonely gull has finally found companions. Bass and treble all take their places—the great gull choir begins!

Treasured Collectibles:

1. Collector’s Edition: Butterfly Dream Amber

2. Prismatic Iris · Sol

3. Prismatic Iris · Lun

4. Prismatic Iris · Dark

5. Collector’s Edition: Ironhelm Shieldguard: Build fear into a solid wall, and turn cowardice into the courage to protect. The hardest enemy to defeat is always the timid self.

6. Collector’s Edition: Songbird Serenade: The mountain wind whistles, the waves beat the rhythm, and the lonely gull has finally found companions. Bass and treble all take their places—the great gull choir begins!

\

1. New season challenge gameplay added. Complete specific challenges to earn achievement rewards.

Complete challenge quests in Operation: Egg Heist Team Mode or Operation: Egg Heist to earn corresponding rewards; complete the "Golden Egg" challenge to obtain the "Departure with the Wind: Collectible Blind Box," which guarantees a season Collectible.

2. New Nightmare and Chaos mode Sanctum maps added.

\

1. Reduced the P.DEF of all Umbral Aniimo in the Sanctum to improve the combat experience of melee Aniimo.

2. Reduced the durability consumption of melee Aniimo's "Protective Unit."

3. "Egg Heist Shop" now sells "Basic Berserker Chip": dealing damage to nearby enemies restores Pathfinder HP.

4. Added the new Alpha "Umbral Bouldus" and its fixed spawn room.

5. Added the new mechanic enemy "Umbral Bubbeep." Defeating it grants a continuous HP recovery effect.

6. Modified the mechanic of "Umbral Baleetle." Successfully breaking free now restores all of the Pathfinder's HP.

7. Reduced the HP of "Umbral Sparki."

8. Added some non-mechanic Umbral Aniimo to enrich spawn randomness.

9. Increased the drop rewards of Prismatic Chests.

10. Newly obtained "Mysterious Prismana Egg," "Umbral Aniimo Egg," and "Ruins Aniimo Egg" after the version update can now hatch Aniimo belonging to Whisperwake Isles.

11. Aniimo Eggs obtained in gameplay can be viewed directly on the settlement screen and are placed directly into Inventory Warehouse, with no need to claim them via mail.

12. Optimized the weapon durability consumption logic for skills with ongoing costs.

13. Added the Unstuck function to external islands.

"Homeland"

Home Season Update

\

「Aniimo-Europe」After the version update ~ 2026/12/10 03:59 (UTC+0)

「Aniimo-Americas」After the version update ~ 2026/12/10 03:59 (UTC-4)

「Aniimo-Apac」After the version update ~ 2026/12/10 03:59 (UTC+8)

2. New season story "The Pumpkin God’s Journey." The mysterious Pumpkin God quietly descends upon Pathfinders' RV Homes! Although it has lost its memory, it seems to have quite a background. What blessings will it bring to Pathfinders?

3. New magical crops "Magic Pumpkin" and "Memory Lanternfruit." Discover and collect different mutated forms of magical crops to light up the Index!

"Crimson Phantom Set": Crimson velvet lays out splendor and elegance. In the quiet, the phantom whispers an invitation to the dark night.

"Sparkling Hue" Feature

1. Interface iteration

Pathfinders can use existing functions such as Sparkle Infusion and Hue Reroll in the brand-new "Sparkling Hue" interface, which also adds two new functions: Hue Swap and Use Legendary Aniipod.

2. Hue unlock and switch

When Pathfinders have caught an Aniimo individual with a certain Sparkling Hue, that hue will be permanently unlocked. Sparkling Hues can also be unlocked randomly by using "Sparkling Pigment."

Pathfinders can preview the unlocked Sparkling Hues of the current Aniimo in the "Hue Swap" interface, and can spend "Credits" to freely switch between different hues of the same Aniimo.

※Hue unlock only applies to the same Aniimo individual and is not shared between species.

3. Hue Reroll

Pathfinders can spend "Sparkling Pigment" to reroll an Aniimo's Sparkling Hue. When a hue that has already been unlocked is rolled, "Sparkling Sigil" ×2 will be returned.

After the version update, the results of each Sparkling Aniimo's Hue Reroll can be viewed in the newly added Reroll Record, with records available for the most recent 3 months.After the version update, we will also reissue the corresponding "Sparkling Sigil" to all Pathfinders who had already rolled duplicate Sparkling Hue types via Hue Reroll before the update. Please watch for in-game mail at that time.

4. Use Legendary Aniipod

Pathfinders can use a "Legendary Aniipod" on a "Sparkling Aniimo." After use, its bound Aniipod will be replaced with that Legendary Aniipod, and the corresponding exclusive Sparkling effect will be obtained.

※Using this function to replace the Legendary Aniipod cannot change the target Aniimo's Acquired Potential.

※This function cannot be used on Irisalis, Helion, or Lunara.

5. New "Sparkling Original"

A new initial color scheme, "Sparkling Original," has been added, with Sparkling effects. Any Sparkling Aniimo can automatically obtain and freely switch to this color scheme.

1. Optimized the Aniimo release interface to reduce the risk of misoperation, and the release list can now be precisely controlled.

2. Switching Aniimo Party will take effect immediately, without needing to tap the deploy button again.

items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

We've heard a lot from you lately about Operation: Egg Heist, from Sanctum exploration and rescuing teammates to Chaos Mode's difficulty and Aniimo Training. We've been following your discussions closely and taking a fresh look at the gameplay experience to figure out what we can improve.

In this Dev Feedback, we're tackling some questions, sharing where things stand and what we're planning next.

Q1: Since the update, why does it feel like we're running into more Aniimo, and they're harder to shake off once they spot us? Why wasn't any of this mentioned in the patch notes?

First, we'd like to clear something up: we haven't made any numerical changes to things like Aniimo (or Chest) spawn probabilities. We're taking a close look at the spawning, combat disengagement, and enemy aggro issues you've reported to see if anything isn't working as intended. If we find a bug, we'll get it fixed as quickly as we can. It might also help to explain a little more about how Aniimo spawns work in the Sanctum. Not all Aniimo appear at the start of a run. As your exploration unfolds, more Aniimo may appear over time. When you dig up rare Aniimo Eggs or Rare Treasure, you disturb dormant Aniimo and attract them over! Any official changes to the game will be documented in our update announcements. We'll also make an effort to give you an earlier heads-up about major upcoming updates, so you know what to expect well in advance.

Q2: Whether you're down and calling for help or trying to rescue a teammate, the experience so far can be really frustrating. Are improvements on the way?

Absolutely! Exploring and fighting are a big part of Operation: Egg Heist, but having each other's backs should matter, too. We know the current rescue experience isn't quite where we'd like it to be, so we're planning new mechanics to make helping a downed teammate easier. We also want to give Pathfinders who go out of their way to help others some well-deserved recognition and rewards. Ultimately, we don't want rescuing a teammate to feel like just another task. We want it to be a rewarding part of working together as a squad, where lending a hand really makes a difference."

Q3: If I'm still missing some Collectibles when S1 ends, will I get another chance to collect them?

You will! We've got new gameplay coming in the second half of S1, giving you more reliable ways to get Collectibles. And even after the season wraps up, we'll bring back Collectibles from previous seasons through future events, so you'll still have plenty of chances to fill in the gaps.

Q4: Chaos Mode feels way too punishing right now. I always get knocked, and there aren't many viable Aniimo or team comps to choose from. Any plans to improve it?

Chaos Mode is meant to be the toughest challenge in squad-based Operation: Egg Heist, where greater risks come with greater rewards. But we don't want higher difficulty to simply mean getting knocked down more often. We want you to have more ways to deal with danger, adapt to different situations, and find strategies that work for you. With that in mind, here's what we're planning based on your feedback:

1. More team composition options We're adding more Aniimo suited to Operation: Egg Heist, opening up new team compositions and strategies for you to experiment with. Keep an eye out for new Aniimo in upcoming updates!

2. More Chip acquisition methods We'll gradually introduce more ways to obtain Chips, including new sources for Heal Chips and Chips that improve the melee combat experience.

3. More ways to tackle challenges in the Sanctum We're planning to introduce more interactive gameplay elements throughout the Sanctum. Like by activating certain mechanisms or defeating specific Aniimo, you'll be able to gain temporary abilities that help you adapt to different combat situations.

4. A more flexible approach to high-difficulty challenges Going forward, high-difficulty content will tend to follow a format similar to the current Limited-Time Challenge, with reasonable rewards. You'll be free to choose whether to take part."

Q5: What's the update plan for Operation: Egg Heist, and how often can we expect new content?

We'll be rolling out major updates each season, alongside smaller updates every two weeks to keep things fresh. Here's a look:

First half of the season: Updates will focus primarily on PvE content. Second half of the season: We'll shift our focus to casual competitive modes. Fresh content every half-season: We'll introduce new Collectibles, along with new maps, Aniimo, and gameplays. Small updates every two weeks: Smaller updates will bring new content, including new Aniimo and their drops, as well as balance tweaks and other adjustments. New Alphas and mobs with unique mechanics: These new foes will bring more variety to combat with their own unique mechanics, and we'll introduce exclusive challenge rewards to go with them.

By combining major seasonal updates with smaller updates every two weeks, we want each stage of Operation: Egg Heist to feel fresh, while giving you new things to collect and new challenges to take on throughout.

Q6: Why doesn't increasing ATK always mean more damage for certain Aniimo?

We believe an Aniimo's role should reflect its specialty in combat, not limit how you choose to train it. Even if an Aniimo isn't particularly good at dealing damage, we still want you to be able to bring it into battle, make the most of its strengths, and enjoy experimenting with different builds. To make this possible, we've built a safeguard into the damage calculation for non-DPS Aniimo. When their ATK is low, they receive an ATK boost based on their level (or their BREAK stat, for BREAK Aniimo) when damage is calculated. This ensures they can still break through enemy defenses rather than struggle to deal damage at all. However, this safeguard comes with a downside. When an Aniimo's ATK falls below the guaranteed minimum, investing more in ATK won't immediately translate into higher damage. This explains why some of you have noticed that your Aniimo's damage stays the same even after boosting its ATK.We understand how confusing this can be. After all, investing in a stat should feel rewarding! That's why we're planning to refine the damage calculation in Version 1.1, so that ATK increases have a more direct impact on damage while keeping the overall combat experience largely unchanged. We'll share the details in an official announcement ahead of the update.

And that wraps up this edition of Dev Feedback, dedicated to Operation: Egg Heist.

Feel free to leave any other questions. We look forward to hearing from you and answering more of them in the future.

The Aniimo Dev Team

items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

Hello everyone! Since Aniimo launched, we’ve been blown away by your love and support. Thank you so much for stepping into Idyll and setting out on this adventure with us. Every hour you play and every kind word you share is what motivates us to keep going.

At the same time, we’ve seen plenty of honest feedback and complaints. Every suggestion, complaint, and question you post on social media, in comment sections, and in community is read and reviewed by our dev team. To us, such feedback shows that you genuinely love Aniimo and want it to get better.

Every so often, we’ll round up the issues you care about and talk about most, and share with you what we think, what we’re changing, and what’s coming next. Here are the top issues this time, along with our progress and plans:

1. Rerolling the same Aniimo keeps giving repeat colors and burns through resources. Can this be improved?

In version 1.1, we’re improving Sparkling Hue rerolls for Sparkling Prismana Aniimo. Once it’s live, you’ll be able to freely switch between any Sparkling Hue you’ve already unlocked for an Aniimo.

2. Some Aniimo already look great in their original Prismana colors. After using a Sparkling Cube, can I keep the original color?

After the version 1.1 update, you’ll be able to switch between all the Sparkling Hue styles unlocked for that Prismana Aniimo, including its original Prismana Hue, so you can switch back any time.

3. Why does my Legendary Irisalis have 88 Potential when someone else’s has 99?

We’ve read through all your feedback. Right now, Irisalis’s Innate Potential is random. Since you can only get this Legendary Aniimo once, having random Potential means the payoff isn’t guaranteed for this rare Aniimo. That’s not the experience we want for you.

So after the version 1.1 update, we’re removing Irisalis’s random Innate Potential and setting it to fixed values: ATK: 10, REGEN: 10, HP: 5, BREAK: 5, M.DEF: 5, P.DEF: 5

Any existing Potential above these values will be converted into Starcryst Essence as compensation. Watch for the version update announcement and in-game mail for the exact conversion rules and amounts.

4. Can I switch a Sparkling Aniimo I already own to a Legendary Aniipod’s exclusive Sparkling effect?

After the version 1.1 update, Legendary Aniipods can be used on Sparkling Aniimo. This replaces the Aniipod it was originally caught with and grants that Legendary Aniipod’s exclusive Sparkling effect.

5. Are there plans to fix lag and overheating on mobile?

We’ve received a lot of feedback on this. A dedicated team is optimizing for popular devices right now to reduce lag and overheating and improve the mobile experience as soon as possible.

6. Support tickets take a long time to get a reply. Can this be faster?

We’re continuing to improve how support works, including upgrading the support system, growing the team, and streamlining internal handoffs so that tickets get answered and resolved faster. Some complex issues require checking account data and working across several teams to find the cause, so they may take longer, but we’ll keep improving. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

7. My Steam/Console account failed to link. What should I do?

Please log in to our Customer Support page.

Under Quick Support Links, click Account Issues. Then select Steam Relink (PSN/Xbox) for both the second-level and third-level categories.

Please submit a support ticket with the following information:

- The platform ID you would like to unlink (e.g., Steam ID)

- The UID you are currently using to contact Customer Support, along with the email address linked to it

- The UID you would like to unlink

- The platform currently linked to the UID you would like to unlink

We will review your request and process it as soon as possible.

We’ll keep reviewing your real experiences and suggestions, and share bug fixes, improvements, mechanic changes, and future plans openly. We’d love to hear more of your feedback, too.

Thank you again to every Pathfinder for your patience and honest feedback. Every message you leave motivates us to keep improving. Have fun and enjoy your time in Idyll!

The Aniimo Dev Team
